mainTopic: How the dispute about extinguishing and kindling coals on שבת is explained, and the start of a new פרק on which kinds of blood are forbidden to eat
overview: The amud opens in the middle of the גמרא's search for the real dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק. The case is a person on שבת who put out some coals and lit others. Three explanations are given. First, he meant to do both acts, and the question is whether הבערה brings a חטאת at all (רבי יוסי versus רבי נתן). Second, רבא says the dispute is about doing the acts in a different order than planned. Third, רב אשי says he meant only to extinguish, so the dispute is about דבר שאין מתכוין (רבי שמעון versus רבי יהודה). Next, two ברייתות disagree about someone who stirs coals to warm himself and they catch fire. The גמרא explains that they follow two sides of the dispute about מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. Then the פרק of ספק אכל חלב ends, and a new משנה lists which kinds of blood a person is liable for eating and which he is not. The גמרא begins with a ברייתא that uses the פסוק 'of bird or of animal' to limit the איסור of blood, and first excludes human blood.

steps.title: First explanation: he intended both, and the תנא קמא follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the person meant both to extinguish and to kindle. The תנא קמא holds like רבי יוסי, who says the Torah singled out הבערה to make it a plain לאו with no חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a case where he intended to extinguish and to kindle. The תנא קמא holds like רבי יוסי, who said: kindling was singled out to teach that it is only a regular prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering what the two תנאים argue about. It says the person wanted to do both acts, so the reason the תנא קמא gives only one חטאת must be something else: he holds that kindling never brings a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he meant to do both, why not two חטאות? According to רבי יוסי, the Torah mentions הבערה separately to teach that it is only a לאו, with no כרת and no חטאת. So only the extinguishing (כיבוי) earns a חטאת, which means one חטאת in total.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא
He intended
To extinguish (the מלאכה of כיבוי)
Kindling a fire, one of the 39 מלאכות
It was singled out to be a plain prohibition (punished only with lashes, no חטאת)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the תנא קמא says kindling is permitted on שבת! It is still forbidden. He only says it is a regular לאו, so it does not bring a חטאת.

phrases.english: For example, where he intended to extinguish and to kindle,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: for the first tanna holds like Rabbi Yosei,
who says: kindling was singled out to be a regular prohibition,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in שמות 35:3, "Do not kindle fire in all your dwellings on the day of שבת."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the first explanation of the מחלוקת, which started before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly do the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק disagree about?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The person intended both acts. The תנא קמא gives one חטאת because, like רבי יוסי, he holds הבערה is only a לאו.

steps.title: First explanation continued: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק follows רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק holds like רבי נתן, who says הבערה was singled out to teach that each מלאכה is counted separately. So kindling brings its own חטאת, which makes two in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק holds like רבי נתן, who said: kindling was singled out to teach that the מלאכות are divided, each counted separately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the first explanation by giving the other side. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק counts two חטאות because he holds kindling is a full מלאכה like any other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי נתן, the Torah lists הבערה on its own to show that each מלאכה brings a separate חטאת. So kindling is a normal מלאכה, and doing both acts brings two חטאות. The whole מחלוקת turns into a dispute about how to read the פסוק of הבערה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was singled out to divide: to teach that each מלאכה brings its own חטאת
Sin offering brought for doing a forbidden act by mistake

steps.whatToRemember: First explanation: he meant to do both acts. ת"ק = רבי יוסי (הבערה is only a לאו, so one חטאת). ראב"צ = רבי נתן (הבערה is a full מלאכה, so two חטאות).

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי נָתָן,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, holds like Rabbi Natan,
who says: kindling was singled out to divide.
phrases.notes: "To divide" means to teach that each מלאכה is counted on its own, so each one brings its own חטאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first explanation by giving the reasoning of the second תנא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק gives two חטאות because, like רבי נתן, he holds הבערה is a full מלאכה.

steps.title: רבא: the dispute is about doing the acts out of the planned order
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the difference between the תנאים is a case where the acts happened in a different order than he planned. He extinguished first, even though he meant to kindle first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the difference between them is about doing it first, meaning doing one act before the other, out of the planned order.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a completely different explanation of the מחלוקת. It has nothing to do with רבי יוסי and רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case, the person planned to light the bottom coals first and only then put out the top ones. In fact the extinguishing came first. The תנא קמא says the extinguishing did not happen the way he planned, so it does not count, and he brings only one חטאת. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says changing the order does not matter, so he brings two.

keyTerms.meaning: To do something first, before something else
There is a difference between them

phrases.english: Rava said:
Doing it first is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: He means: the extinguishing happened before the kindling, even though the person planned it the other way around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the same מחלוקת, replacing the one in steps 1–2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנאים disagree when the acts happened out of the planned order. ת"ק says one חטאת, ראב"צ says two.

steps.title: רב אשי: he only meant to extinguish, so this is the מחלוקת about דבר שאין מתכוין
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the person only meant to put out the fire, and the bottom coals lit by themselves. The תנא קמא follows רבי שמעון (an unintended result is פטור). רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק follows רבי יהודה (an unintended result is חייב).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: this is a case where he intended to extinguish, and the coals ignited on their own. The תנא קמא holds like רבי שמעון, who said an unintended act is exempt. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק holds like רבי יהודה, who said an unintended act is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third explanation. This time the person never wanted the kindling at all, and the תנאים are arguing about whether you are responsible for a result you did not intend.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the kindling is a side effect the person did not plan. רבי שמעון holds that דבר שאין מתכוין is פטור, so only the extinguishing counts, and he brings one חטאת. רבי יהודה holds that he is חייב even for the unintended result, so he brings two.

keyTerms.meaning: And they caught fire by themselves (he did not plan it)
An act whose forbidden result the person did not intend
Exempt, not liable
Liable, obligated

steps.whatToRemember: Three ways to explain one מחלוקת: (1) he meant both acts, and the question is whether הבערה is a לאו or a full מלאכה (רבי יוסי / רבי נתן). (2) רבא: the acts happened out of the planned order. (3) רב אשי: he only meant to extinguish, and the question is דבר שאין מתכוין (רבי שמעון / רבי יהודה).
steps.whyThisMatters: רב אשי ties this ברייתא to the famous מחלוקת of רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה about דבר שאין מתכוין, a basic principle of הלכות שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
For example, where he intended to extinguish
and they ignited by themselves,
phrases.notes: "They" are the bottom coals. They caught fire while he was putting out the top ones, without his meaning it.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: and the first tanna holds like Rabbi Shimon,
who says: an unintended act is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: an unintended act is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּתְכַּוֵּין לְכַבּוֹת וְהוּבְעֲרוּ מֵאֵילֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation of the מחלוקת, different from both the first explanation and רבא's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He only intended to extinguish. ת"ק follows רבי שמעון (דבר שאין מתכוין is פטור, so one חטאת). ראב"צ follows רבי יהודה (חייב, so two חטאות).

steps.title: Two teachings disagree about stirring coals that catch fire
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes someone who stirs coals on שבת to warm himself, and they catch fire by themselves. One ברייתא says חייב, another says פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if someone stirs coals on שבת to warm himself, and they catch fire by themselves, one ברייתא says he is liable and another says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows us two ברייתות that rule opposite ways on the same case. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains why they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person only wanted warmth, and the fire started on its own. Two teachings give opposite answers about whether he broke שבת by kindling. So we need a reason for the split.

keyTerms.meaning: One who stirs or rakes coals
To warm oneself
One teaching says this, and the other teaching says that (two sources that contradict)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who stirs coals on Shabbat
in order to warm himself with them
and they caught fire by themselves:
one teaching says: he is liable,
and the other teaching says: he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: חַיָּיב, וְתָנֵי אִידַּךְ: פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the case of putting out a fire to a related שבת case about coals that catch fire by themselves.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about stirring coals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give opposite rulings on the exact same case.

steps.title: The two teachings disagree about a מלאכה not needed for its own sake
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that says חייב holds that a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה is חייב. The one that says פטור holds that it is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The teaching that says liable holds that a מלאכה not needed for its own purpose still makes one liable. The teaching that says exempt holds that such a מלאכה makes one exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. The two ברייתות follow two different opinions about one general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person did not want the fire for the normal purpose of a burning fire. He only wanted warmth. Whether he is liable depends on how you rule on a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, and each ברייתא follows a different side.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden act on שבת done for a purpose other than the act's own normal goal
He holds (this is his opinion)
Liable for it
Exempt for it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Step 4. There the issue was a result the person did not intend at all. Here the גמרא explains the dispute using a different idea: a מלאכה that is not needed for its own purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות about the coals do not really contradict each other. Each one follows a different side of the dispute about מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.

phrases.english: The one that teaches: liable,
holds:
a forbidden labor that is not needed for its own sake,
one is liable for it.
And the one that teaches: exempt,
holds: a forbidden labor that is not needed for its own sake,
one is exempt for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each source to a different opinion (a dispute between תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות contradict each other on the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow two different views on whether a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה makes one חייב.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter on doubtful eating of forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of פרק ספק אכל חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'ספק אכל חלב'.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional goodbye to a finished chapter. The discussion of this פרק is now over, and the next step opens a new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a פרק)
The name of the chapter that is ending: 'He was unsure if he ate forbidden fat'

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'He was unsure if he ate forbidden fat'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter of ספק אכל חלב is finished.

steps.title: Kinds of blood that make a person liable
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists the blood a person is liable for eating. This includes slaughter blood from any animal or bird, kosher or not, and also blood from stabbing, from ripping, and from bloodletting that causes death.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone ate blood from slaughtering a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird, whether kosher or non-kosher, or blood from stabbing, or blood from ripping out the windpipe, or blood from bloodletting that the life goes out with, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It lists the kinds of blood for which eating carries full liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What these kinds of blood share is that they are the blood the animal's life goes out with. It does not matter whether the animal is kosher or how it died. If the blood is the life-blood, a person is liable for eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that comes out during slaughter
Blood from stabbing the animal (killing it without proper slaughter)
Blood from ripping out the windpipe or food pipe
Blood from bloodletting
That the life goes out with

phrases.english: MISHNA: If one ate blood of slaughter,
of a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird,
whether non-kosher or kosher,
blood of stabbing, blood of ripping,
blood of bloodletting
that the life goes out with,
one is liable for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating life-blood (from slaughter, stabbing, ripping, or deadly bloodletting) of any animal or bird makes one liable.

steps.title: Kinds of blood that do not make a person liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists blood with no liability: blood of the spleen, heart, eggs, grasshoppers, and oozing blood. רבי יהודה makes one liable for the oozing blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood of the spleen, blood of the heart, blood of eggs, blood of grasshoppers, and blood that oozes out — one is not liable for these. רבי יהודה makes one liable for the oozing blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite list, the kinds of blood that do not bring liability. It ends with a dispute about one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These kinds of blood are not the main life-blood. Some is blood found inside organs, some comes from eggs or insects, and some is the slow drip after the main spurt. רבי יהודה disagrees only about the slow oozing blood, דם התמצית, and he holds it does bring liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that slowly oozes out after the main spurt of slaughter
Blood of the spleen
Grasshoppers
One is not liable for it

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה divides blood into two groups. Life-blood brings liability. Organ blood, egg blood, insect blood, and oozing blood do not, but רבי יהודה says oozing blood does.

phrases.english: Blood of the spleen, blood of the heart,
blood of eggs, blood of grasshoppers,
blood that oozes out,
one is not liable for it.
Rabbi Yehuda holds one liable for blood that oozes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה by giving the list of blood that brings no liability, the opposite of Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of the spleen, heart, eggs, grasshoppers, and oozing blood bring no liability. רבי יהודה says oozing blood does.

steps.title: Does 'all blood' include every kind of blood?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that the words כל דם might include human blood, egg blood, grasshopper blood and fish blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the פסוק says 'You shall eat no blood.' I might think this means all blood, even human blood, egg blood, grasshopper blood and fish blood. Is everything included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts by raising a possible reading: maybe 'all blood' really means every kind of blood. This is a setup, and the next step will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כל (all) sounds like it covers every type of blood with no limit. The ברייתא lists the blood types that seem least likely to be meant, to ask whether even these are forbidden. This explains why the משנה (Step 9) left some blood types out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall eat no blood': the פסוק that forbids eating blood
'I might understand': a first possible reading before the real answer
Two-legged walkers, meaning human beings
Is everything included?

phrases.english: Gemara. The Rabbis taught:
"You shall eat no blood" (literally, 'all blood you shall not eat')

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אֲפִילּוּ דַּם מְהַלְּכֵי שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: I might understand that this includes even the blood of two-legged walkers,
phrases.notes: 'Two-legged walkers' is the ברייתא's way of saying people.

phrases.aramaic: דַּם בֵּיצִים, דַּם חֲגָבִים, דַּם דָּגִים,
phrases.english: the blood of eggs, the blood of grasshoppers, the blood of fish,
is everything included?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the new משנה by looking for the source behind the משנה's list of which blood is forbidden.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the word כל in the פסוק include every kind of blood, even human, egg, grasshopper and fish blood?

steps.title: Only blood like bird and animal blood is included
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the words לעוף ולבהמה: only creatures that share the special features of birds and animals are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'of bird or of animal.' Birds and animals are special in three ways. They can have a light טומאה and a severe טומאה. Some are forbidden and some are permitted. They are a type of meat. So anything that has these features is included too.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. The פסוק itself names birds and animals, so 'all blood' is limited to creatures similar to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three features that birds and animals share. First, they can carry both a light טומאה and a severe טומאה. Second, some kinds are forbidden and some are permitted. Third, they count as meat. Only blood from a creature with all of these features falls under the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches': introduces the words that answer the question
'Just as these are special, so too anything like them': a way of extending a rule to similar cases
A light type of ritual impurity
A severe type of ritual impurity
Forbidden and permitted kinds
A type of meat

steps.confusionAlert: The last line only mentions 'light טומאה,' but it is a short way of saying it. It means anything that has all the features just listed, like birds and animals.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three features are the test the ברייתא will use to decide which blood types from Step 10 are left out.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Of bird or of animal,"
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק, ויקרא 7:26.

phrases.english: just as birds and animals are special

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן טוּמְאָה קַלָּה וְטוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה,
phrases.english: in that they can have a light impurity and a severe impurity,
and among them there are forbidden and permitted kinds,
and they are a type of meat,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן טוּמְאָה קַלָּה.
phrases.english: so too, anything that can have a light impurity (along with the other features) is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 by limiting 'all blood' to creatures like birds and animals.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only blood from creatures that, like birds and animals, can have both a light and a severe טומאה, have forbidden and permitted kinds, and are a type of meat.

steps.title: Human blood is excluded
steps.stepSummary: Human blood is excluded, because people can have a severe טומאה but not a light טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So I leave out human blood. People can have a severe טומאה, but they cannot have a light טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses the test from Step 11 for the first time. It takes human blood out of the איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who dies carries the severe טומאה of a dead body. But the human body never counts as food that becomes impure, so it cannot have the light טומאה. Since humans are missing this feature, their blood is not included in the איסור of eating blood.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I will exclude': taking something out of the rule

phrases.english: I will exclude the blood of two-legged walkers,
since they can have a severe impurity,
but they cannot have a light impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the test from Step 11 to the first item listed in Step 10, human blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Human blood is not included in the איסור of eating blood, because humans cannot have the light type of טומאה.
